articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Consumer Applications of Radar and Sonar' (Digest No.124)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Consumer Applications of Radar and Sonar
IEE Colloquium on Consumer Applications of Radar and Sonar
abstract: Investigates applications of microwave radar in the automotive environment. Many of these applications are considered by reviewing work at Lucas that has been conducted over the last 25 years. Applications investigated are obstacle detection and avoidance, longitudinal vehicle control, improved vehicle dynamics and instrumentation. In each case, the technologies are described and results presented that show the advantages and disadvantages of the microwave techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Consumer Applications of Radar and Sonar
abstract: To both professional and amateur divers, navigation underwater in reduced visibility, or in a current or tideway, can be a daunting business. The paper explores some of the options that are available for extending or improving the divers sensory envelope and navigational capability in such conditions, and presents some new equipment ideas that have evolved from the author's work in this field.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A precise short range radar for anti-collision systems with automatic braking
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Consumer Applications of Radar and Sonar
abstract: In any anti-collision application where automatic braking is applied in response to detection of a collision risk, a very high probability of detection must be accompanied by a very low level of false alarms. The paper describes a radar specially developed for reverse protection on quarry vehicles, which has now been adapted for a variety of other applications where its special features are particularly useful.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Consumer Applications of Radar and Sonar
abstract: A simple solution to the problem of forming many beams at acoustic imaging frequencies is provided by acoustic mirror technology. The Fourier transform required to achieve imaging is performed geometrically by appropriate shaping of the mirror as in optics. The design of an underwater acoustic imaging system is described. To minimise cost personal computer based commercial software is used. The characteristics of the system built are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Systems and processing considerations for consumer radar applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Consumer Applications of Radar and Sonar
abstract: Recent innovations in both the fields of radar and signal processing have made quite complex consumer radar systems possible. The paper examines the systems and processing requirements for a typical example and considers the general issues that arise from it. At present, the major potential areas for radar in consumer products are: Doppler radar speedometers, radar based intelligent cruise control (radar cruise), radar based obstacle detection systems for cars and in the security field. Radar cruise is taken as the prime example as it encompasses most of the more difficult systems and processing issues. After considering this example, it goes on to examine the general consumer product requirements which are of particular relevance to radar systems and the requirements of a radar system which are peculiar in the consumer market. It also considers the systems and processing considerations for placing a radar in a safety related system and what cost performance trade offs should be considered in producing a marketable product.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
